name: Yemen

findings.summary: The internationally recognised government inaugurated AdenNet in Aden in June 2018, a USD 100m ISP and 4G package built with UAE funding and Chinese equipment, giving it internet capacity independent of Houthi-run YemenNet.
findings.analyst_inference: Authority: Aden-based internationally recognised government. Equipment vendor rule gives pole prc, but only Foreign Policy says 'Chinese equipment' and names no firm; Debriefer gives the USD 100m figure (package incl. Aden gateway and Aden 4G) and no vendor. Recorded Future (2019) says AdenNet saw little adoption, so tier 4 not 5. No S1/S2 source confirms the vendor: uncorroborated, low. still_current not checked.

findings.local_actor: Not stated (Recorded Future says 'Yemen'; CEP relays it as YemenNet, Houthi-controlled Sanaa)
findings.summary: A 2019 Recorded Future study reports that Yemen bought a large amount of telecommunications equipment from Huawei; the purchasing entity, date, value and equipment type are not given.
findings.analyst_inference: Date is the report date, not the purchase date. Authority unclear: Recorded Future does not say whether the buyer was Sanaa (Houthi) or Aden; CEP attributes it to YemenNet, which is Houthi-controlled. Tier 3 assumes a completed purchase; no counterparty contract seen. CEP echoes Recorded Future, so not independent. Low.

findings.summary: Citizen Lab found Netsweeper filtering on YemenNet after the Houthi takeover of Sanaa, blocking political, independent media and all .il sites; Recorded Future identified further Netsweeper devices on YemenNet in 2019.
findings.analyst_inference: Authority: Houthi-controlled Sanaa institutions. Filtering appliances classed as network equipment; Netsweeper (Canadian) supplies and updates them, so pole third. Two independent opened S2 sources four years apart. Pre-2020; not reconfirmed as current, so still_current null. Citizen Lab notes US vendor Websense withdrew from Yemeni ISPs after 2009.

findings.summary: The internationally recognised government signed a five-year Starlink licence in January 2024, running to January 2029; Starlink announced service availability in Yemen in September 2024, with kits around USD 389.
findings.analyst_inference: Authority: internationally recognised government; licensing ministry not named in sources opened. Tier 4 (licence issued, service launched); subscriber scale unknown, so not tier 5. Global Voices gives licence terms, Total Telecom the launch date; they are independent but neither is S1.

findings.local_actor: Houthi Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (Sanaa)
findings.summary: Houthi authorities in Sanaa banned Starlink, calling it a US espionage and war tool, threatened sellers with jail, and in April 2025 ordered residents to surrender terminals or face security investigation.
findings.analyst_inference: Authority: Houthi de facto government, so scale subnational (territory it controls). Reversal at tier of the licensed service; reason geopolitical per stated US-threat rationale. Ban date not stated; date is the surrender order reported April 2025.

facilities.null_reason: one search found no data-centre or AI-campus project since 2023 under either authority

silicon.null_reason: no dedicated search; no accelerator purchase surfaced in other searches; conflict and sanctions context makes one unlikely

models.null_reason: one search found no frontier-model partnership or sovereign model for either authority

applications.null_reason: one search on Houthi surveillance cameras/Hikvision found nothing Yemen-specific; DPI purchase by TeleYemen reported (CEP relaying UN Panel) without vendor

research_gaps: Vendor of the 'bandwidth management system' (DPI) bought by Houthi-controlled TeleYemen per the 2022 UN Panel of Experts report, and whether deployed.
Named vendor and current status of AdenNet / Aden 4G equipment (Huawei vs ZTE) and whether AdenNet still operates.
Huawei purchase cited by Recorded Future 2019: buyer (YemenNet/PTC Sanaa vs Aden), date, value, equipment type.
RAN/core vendors of Yemen Mobile, YOU (ex-MTN Yemen), Sabafon and Y-Telecom, and how the 2021 move of an operator HQ to Aden affected them.
Licensing ministry and instrument for the January 2024 Starlink licence (S1 source), and Starlink subscriber numbers.
Whether Netsweeper filtering on YemenNet continued after 2019.
Submarine cable landings (AAE-1, FALCON, etc.) and post-2024 Red Sea repairs; any PRC-built cable or HMN Tech role; Aden government probe of AAE-1 repair delays (SubTel Forum, not opened).
